title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 92
paragraphs: As regards marvels worth recording, the land of Lydia has no great store of them compared with other lands, apart from the gold-dust that is carried down from Tmolus; but one work it has to show that is larger by far than any other, except only those in Egypt and Babylon. For there stands there the sepulchral monument of Alyattes, father of Croesus, of which the base is made of larger stones and the rest of the monument is of earth piled up. This was built by contributions of those who practiced trade, of the artisans, and of the girls who plied their traffic there. And even in my own time there still existed upon the monument above five boundary-stones, on which were carved inscriptions telling how much of the work had been done by each class; and upon measurement it was found that the work of the girls was the greatest in amount. For the daughters of the common people in Lydia all practice prostitution to gather dowries for themselves, continuing this until the time when they marry, and the girls give themselves away in marriage. Now the circuit of the monument is six stades and two hundred feet, and the breadth is thirteen hundred feet. Adjoining the monument is a great lake, which the Lydians say has a never-failing supply of water, and it is called the lake of Gyges. Such is the nature of this monument.
